approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh pool of molecular graphs from molecules already scored in the current session. A Gaussian process over integer molecular fingerprints supplies ten persistent sampled functions. Each function guides eight waves of graph edits through a four-member beam, retaining values for every visited graph. Once all paths finish, stalled sessions restrict each path to its forty highest posterior-mean graphs. The Parent buys distinct maxima of the same sampled functions that guided expansion, then learns and breeds only from real feedback.
approach.novelty: Use a fresh, independent posterior function to judge each completed path and choose its purchase. The guiding functions still construct exactly the same paths on the same inputs, and the successful final mean screen stays in place. This changes the dependence between construction and purchase while preserving the posterior model and correlation within each field. The sibling source screen restricted intermediate graph options and reduced useful full-session gain; this intervention preserves those options and changes only which completed options are bought.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-dc60d82e4f36 has a productive-search bottleneck after correctly executed coherent expansion: the function optimized to construct a field also chooses its paid maximum. Complete Parent Search evidence records 3804/4350 purchases with zero positive gain over their real scored generating roots, mean purchased sampled optimism 0.14096400677019458, and 3081 nonterminal purchases without a later accepted descendant. Its final mean screen is a confirmed capability: full equal-session positive root gain is 0.0035516224072537706, above its own Parent n-eb15da16dbea at 0.0030352346989319977, and macro endpoint mean is 0.5780299607734479 (available-seed population SD 0.012491926868813345). The source-screen sibling n-452bf85f3c43 changed 35362 source draws and 350 paid ancestries, but full root gain fell to 0.003365321651016045 despite endpoint delta +0.00045362963725429733. The Parent has 61 paid routes through sources that screen would exclude, including 14 root beaters. This supports testing independence at final purchase while preserving graph support; it does not prove that reused guide noise causes optimism or that a new judge must help. The formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains a separate comparator with mean 0.607030316211131. Exact source/hash and per-session audit reuse are recorded in policy/scratch/r0078-01-improve-L01/plan/evidence-review.json.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the ticket's exact frozen Search Policy review and position2 adoption/deviation record at policy/scratch/search_policy-146d13ebf75c/literature-adoptions.json. Its recorded discovery queries are inherited; this PLAN ran no new search queries and opened the two already cited primary papers to check applicability. Wilson's finite Gaussian conditioning/sampling law supports a checkable exact draw on the bounded completed field. The guide/judge independence hypothesis is an internal-evidence adaptation and neither the paper's approximate prior/data decomposition nor a performance guarantee. Double Q-learning is read only as a selection-bias caution: this method has no independently fitted Bellman value estimators and imports no unbiasedness or convergence theorem. Preserve the Parent GP, full covariance, residual scale and canonical aliases. B1/B3 bottleneck review supports this concrete consumer change, not continuation by literature prestige. No new model, dependency or preparation input is needed.

hypothesis: Change only the coupling between guide-driven domain construction and final purchase. Given the current real accepted-data fit D, let G_j be each path's complete canonical graph field after every guiding path has finished. Freeze G_j, its guide values and the inherited real-mean eligibility set E_j. On distinct exact count-feature identities in G_j draw one new vector J_j = mu_D(G_j) + score_scale * F_D(G_j) z_j, with F F^T equal to the full inherited standardized latent posterior covariance and fresh independent z_j. Judge innovations are independent of all expansion-guiding innovations and of other paths' judge innovations; the moments depend on accepted data and the frozen locations, never on guide sample values. The adaptively chosen field still depends on the guide, so no unconditional independence of observed guide/judge scores on selected fields is claimed. Buy the highest J_j in E_j excluding actual earlier purchased/seen canonical identities, using original path order and ascending canonical identity ties. Retain correlated residual magnitude and the final K3/M40 screen; no source restriction, averaging, predictor replacement or extra graph search is introduced. The testable causal hypothesis is that a fresh judge reduces the control of guide-specific optimistic excursions over purchases while retaining the full graph options, thereby increasing real positive root gain. Maximizing the judge can still select optimistic residuals; no general bias-removal result is assumed.

finding_summary.headline: Independent judging changed purchases, but full root gain and endpoint score fell
finding_summary.insights:
This separates valid decoupling from useful transfer. Exact posterior moments, preserved guide construction and thousands of changed purchases rule out absent exposure or a failed sampler as explanations for this result. The retained finite Gaussian sampling element operated, but the borrowed mathematics supplies no benefit guarantee for choosing a new maximum on an adaptively built field. Lower sampled optimism, more root beaters, more later-used products and better late gain did not produce greater full-session gain. This settles the registered independent-judging intervention on this host; it leaves the confirmed final screen, other acquisition methods and the wider approach open.

The purchase stream became much shallower despite retaining graph-expansion support: base-field purchases rose from 954 to 2,849, and mean paid extension depth fell from 1.78 to 0.57. This is a measured change in which constructed options were bought, not evidence that the unbought guide alternatives would have scored better. Among 19,456 untied co-purchased pairs, the judge ordered 48.1% correctly, while the real GP mean ordered 70.4%. The judge still overpredicted 4,011 purchased outcomes, 3,699 purchases failed to beat their roots, and 2,913 nonterminal products never became a root of a later accepted purchase. Those measurements identify persistent limitations in ranking useful improvements and turning structural exploration into substantial gains; they do not establish a calibration cause or a mediation path. A different predictive ranking model or a proposal/search method that preserves and revisits supported core structures could address those limitations, but its benefit is untested here.

The chemistry supports that diagnosis without identifying the cause of the score loss. Fragment-sized products increased from 61 to 103 and products with at least 50 heavy atoms from 217 to 428, even as the median size fell. Fragment-excluded nearest-neighbor similarity increased in all five task populations, and some upper-score bands concentrated in fewer generic cores; other bands broadened, so this is not universal scaffold collapse. Unusual heteroatom attachments and unspecified stereochemistry remain. These observations motivate context-sensitive, core-preserving graph operations and controlled access to distinct supported cores, not a universal size cutoff, chemistry penalty or claim that any unseen alternative is superior.
finding_summary.results:
The independent judges ran correctly across all fifteen Search sessions and changed 4,117 of 4,350 paid choices. All real labels reached feedback, including 4,200 next-fit uses and 150 terminal censors. The full-panel positive gain over generating roots fell from 0.00355162 to 0.00279595 per purchase, with lower averages on all three seeds. This triggers the registered useful-transfer falsifier. Seven task/seed cells improved and eight worsened. More purchases beat their roots—651 versus 546—but their total positive gain was smaller. Late gain increased from 0.00188030 to 0.00217048, and average purchased sampled optimism fell from 0.140964 to 0.085846; both are secondary improvements that cannot replace the full-panel test.

Final mean score fell from 0.578030 to 0.529067, a paired difference of −0.048963; the separate formal Anchor remains at 0.607030. The largest adverse cell was drd2 seed 1, with a −0.733553 endpoint difference. Seed-level macro differences were −0.019920, −0.148382 and +0.021413. Both baseline comparisons pass the protocol's uncertainty-sensitive task-regression rule, which does not establish reliability. The independent +0.002 score target was missed, and the formal-Anchor-as-code-Parent criterion does not apply to this descendant. Judging cost averaged 19.4 seconds per session, mostly receipt logging; every task completed within its limit.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output retains unusual attachments and undefined stereochemistry; both tiny fragments and oversized graphs increase
molecular.overall_character: The frozen comparison separately confirms complete Child evaluation and complete pairing with actual code Parent n-dc60d82e4f36. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent Search trajectories were read; there are no missing paired paths or uncovered tasks. No separate chemistry comparison to the formal Anchor is made. Each task supplies 870 accepted optimizer products, for 4,350 per node; the ten initial records in each session are retained separately. These trajectories describe purchased outputs, not every internally considered graph. The molecules include compact fused heteroarenes and aryl carboxamides, halogenated diaryl aminoalkyl compounds, nitrogen-rich cyclic carbonyl/imino systems, and extensive fused, bridged and spiro connectivity. The digest ring-marker rates are 0.9701 to 0.9828 and aromatic-marker rates 0.9575 to 0.9805. These rates describe strings containing markers, not proportions of aromatic atoms or perceived ring counts. RDKit finds rings in 4,245 and aromatic atoms in 4,217 products. Median heavy-atom count is 29 versus Parent 31, yet both tails expand: 103 products have at most six heavy atoms and 428 have at least fifty, versus Parent 61 and 217; maxima are 120 versus 113. Thus a smaller median does not imply better control of graph size. Nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and oxygen-oxygen bonds occur in 877, 756 and 81 products, versus Parent 999, 656 and 287. These directions are mixed and the motifs also occur in some upper-score bands. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups are present: 2,019 products match the declared nonamide-amine connectivity proxy, 926 with a ring match; zero formal charges do not establish absent ionizability. The complete output has 2,016 typed and 1,245 generic nonempty Murcko scaffolds, versus Parent 2,265 and 1,345. This is broad graph exploration with conditional upper-band concentration, not universal scaffold collapse. All five within-task nearest-neighbor means increase after excluding products with at most six heavy atoms; per-task values and same-seed Child-to-Parent comparisons are retained in the audits. Similarity uses 2048-bit radius-two Morgan fingerprints without chirality; shared identities across seeds are retained and the statistic is a representation-dependent description, not an independent diversity experiment. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2,976 products versus Parent 3,230, with assigned centres in zero for both. Potential unspecified double-bond stereo occurs in 1,290 versus 1,181, with zero specified double-bond stereo in both; this additional exposure uses RDKit experimental stereo perception and is not a count of realizable or stable stereoisomers. The small-all-aromatic-ring review flag occurs in 177 versus 98 products. The audit log contains approximate-ring-finding warnings; ring and scaffold readings are toolkit graph diagnostics, not three-dimensional geometry certificates. No synthetic route, stability measurement, pKa, conformer assessment, stereoisomer comparison or biological efficacy is supplied. The upper/lower score bands each contain 29 products per session or 87 per pooled task, selected only from recorded scores with deterministic ties; all early and late purchases and both size tails remain in the audit. The uppercase-carbon carbonyl/amide SMARTS do not count every aromatic lactam. The generic cumulated-double query also matches sulfonyl O=S=O and must not be interpreted as a count of allenes or reactive cumulenes. Score-gradient readings are chemical associations within observed adaptive streams, not hidden-target reconstruction, component contribution, activation judgments or causal explanations of paired endpoint changes. Definitions, exact input paths and original/copy hashes: policy/scratch/r0078-01-improve-L01/molecular/evidence-manifest.json; derived counts and all score bands: policy/scratch/r0078-01-improve-L01/molecular/descriptor-summary.json. Toolkit messages: policy/scratch/r0078-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit.log.

liabilities: N-halogenated amides, N-N substitution, N-O substitution and halomethyl groups merit local reactivity and route review. Thirty-five upper-band products contain N-halogen bonds, so their presence cannot be treated as a universal observed score penalty.

Twenty-four products have at most six heavy atoms versus Parent twenty; none reaches fifty heavy atoms. Tiny late products and the poorly scoring larger connected examples demonstrate both contraction and expansion liabilities without supporting a fixed size cutoff.
missing_features: Weak products often fail to retain the compact intact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement found in the upper band; aromatic rings and ordinary amide groups are already well represented overall.

The upper output provides few alternative core arrangements with equally supported scores and consistently ordinary N-substitution; no unseen target scaffold or particular halogen requirement can be inferred.

Configuration is absent in the 83 products with perceived tetrahedral centres, while the upper 87 have none; stereochemistry is therefore an output capability gap here, not an evidenced explanation of the leading scores.

Seed-1 products at evaluations 229, 241 and 246 all score 0.46092619585962435 despite replacing the halomethyl halogen among F, Cl and Br. The upper 87 occupy 23 to 26 heavy atoms, all have three rings and a carbonyl-proxy match, and 70 have an amide match, versus 44 carbonyl and 38 amide matches in the lower 87. The seed-2 ketone leader at evaluation 259 scores 0.4572645941803378, so an amide is not universal among favorable observed products. The 47-heavy-atom expanded aromatic amide at seed 2 evaluation 36 scores 2.8380167321919517e-13, while the tiny imine C=NF at seed 1 evaluation 115 scores zero. Both loss of the core through contraction and excessive linked-core growth can be poor even when the local graph is valid; the actual SMILES are single components. The final seed-2 azo/N-F-substituted amide scores 0.2626354797426377 and is not the incumbent. The upper band covers 13 typed/eight generic scaffolds versus Parent 33/seven.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
